key_insight: Laser post-treatment reduced wear rates by approximately 24% for detonation-sprayed coatings and 39% for gas-flame-sprayed coatings, while producing deposition-dependent mechanical changes.
engineering_relevance: Laser post-treatment offers a route to more wear-resistant Ni–Cr–Fe–Si–B–C coatings on AISI 321 stainless steel, with stiffness trade-offs depending on the spraying method.
method: Deposit coatings by detonation spraying and gas-flame spraying.
Compare untreated and laser-treated microstructures and phases using SEM, EDS, and XRD.
Measure hardness, elastic modulus, friction, and ball-on-disk wear.
evidence_signal: Detonation-sprayed coating hardness increased from 1049.1 to 1206.1 HV; wear rates fell from 1.939 to 1.465 and from 2.419 to 1.476 × 10⁻⁴ mm³/(N·m) for detonation and gas-flame spraying, respectively.
watch_item: Laser treatment lowered the gas-flame-sprayed coating’s elastic modulus from 228.0 to 187.0 GPa, so wear gains should be weighed against application-specific stiffness requirements.
paper_title: Effect of Laser Post-Treatment on the Microstructure, Mechanical and Tribological Properties of Detonation- and Flame-Sprayed Ni–Cr–Fe–Si–B–C Coatings
